title: OpenStax reports that three-week-olds sucked harder for their mother's voice
summary: OpenStax reports that three-week-old babies sucked more strongly when a pacifier played their mother's voice than a stranger's voice.
body: OpenStax Psychology says that in one experiment, three-week-old babies were given pacifiers that played a recording of the mother's voice and of a stranger's voice. When the infants heard the mother's voice, they sucked more strongly. The textbook cites Mills and Melhuish (1974). This card did not open that paper. The report is about recognizing a familiar voice in that study. It is not a description of how hearing works. The 1974 paper was not opened, so the claim is the textbook's report of the pacifier recording.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 9.3 Stages of Development
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology web page, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports the pacifier study as OpenStax reports it: stronger sucking for the mother's voice at three weeks, citing Mills and Melhuish 1974.
